new_statements.quote: Most Lojban words are stressed on the next-to-the-last, or penultimate, syllable. In counting syllables, however, syllables whose vowel is y or which contain a syllabic consonant (l, m, n, or r) are never counted. [...] Similarly, syllables created solely by adding a buffer vowel, such as [ɪ], are not counted. [...] Primary stress is required on the penultimate syllable of Lojban content words (called brivla). Lojbanized names may be stressed on any syllable, but if a syllable other than the penultimate is stressed, the syllable (or at least its vowel) must be capitalized in writing. Lojban structural words (called cmavo) may be stressed on any syllable or none at all.
new_statements.citation: Cowan, John Woldemar. 2016. The Complete Lojban Language, version 1.1. Fairfax, VA: The Logical Language Group.
new_statements.locator: Chapter 3, Section 3.9 'Syllabication And Stress', p. 43 (PDF p. 43); corroborated ch. 4 sec. 4.3 p. 52 (brivla property 3) and sec. 4.2 p. 52 (cmavo).
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Held file (584 pp., text layer, title page 'The Complete Lojban Language / John Woldemar Cowan / A Logical Language Group Publication / Version 1.1, Generated 2016-08-26') opened with extracted text. Section 3.9 'Syllabication And Stress' runs pp. 42-44; on printed p. 43 (= PDF p. 43) the quoted passage appears word for word: 'Most Lojban words are stressed on the next-to-the-last, or penultimate, syllable. In counting syllables, however, syllables whose vowel is y or which contain a syllabic consonant (l, m, n, or r) are never counted. (The Lojban term for penultimate stress is da'amoi terbasna.) Similarly, syllables created solely by adding a buffer vowel, such as [ɪ], are not counted....…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary word stress falls on the penultimate syllable, where syllables whose nucleus is schwa (y), a syllabic consonant, or an epenthetic buffer vowel are skipped in the count. This is obligatory (and word-boundary-defining) for content words (brivla); names (cmene) default to penult but may bear lexically marked stress elsewhere (written with capitals); function words (cmavo) have no required stress (convention: first vowel of disyllabic cmavo), except that a stressed syllable immediately before a brivla must be followed by a pause.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Three levels (primary, secondary, weak). Secondary stress is 'optional and non-distinctive', used for emphasis/contrast, follows speakers' native habits, and must never create a false primary stress inside a brivla. Weak (no) stress is required on syllables with y, a syllabic consonant, or a buffer vowel.
new_statements.exceptions: Syllables with y, syllabic l/m/n/r, or buffer vowels are invisible to the count and can never be stressed; cmene may carry non-penultimate stress if marked by capitalization (e.g..ARMstrong.); cmavo are free (any syllable or none); primary stress may not fall on a syllable directly preceding a brivla unless a pause intervenes.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level, prescriptive (designed language): stress is part of the word-resolution (parsing) algorithm, so penultimate stress on brivla is definitional. Statement covers citation and connected-speech forms alike; phrase-level emphasis is relegated to optional secondary stress.
new_statements.identity_note: Lojban (jbo, lojb1234), the LLG-defined logical language (offshoot of Loglan, logl1234 is a distinct Glottolog entry). CLL is the language's official defining reference grammar, so the stress rule is prescriptive/definitional rather than a field description; no dialect issue.
